Pool a prespecified Cox proportional hazards analysis of completed datasets

Source: R/analysis.R
catmech_pool_coxph.Rd

Fits a Cox proportional hazards model ([survival::coxph()]) across each completed dataset and pools parameter estimates and standard errors using Rubin's rules with Barnard & Rubin (1999) small-sample degrees of freedom based on event counts.

Usage

catmech_pool_coxph(
  result,
  formula,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  allow_sensitivity = FALSE,
  cluster = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

result

A `catmech_result` from [catmech_model()], [catmech_pmm()], [catmech_reference()], [catmech_contamination()] or [catmech_impute()].

formula

A prespecified formula for [survival::coxph()] (e.g. `Surv(time, status) ~ lab_value + age`).

conf_level

Confidence level between zero and one (default 0.95).

exponentiate

Logical: if `TRUE` (default), adds exponentiated estimates and confidence intervals (`estimate_exp`, `lower_exp`, `upper_exp`), representing Hazard Ratios (HR).

allow_sensitivity

Explicitly allow pooled calculations for sensitivity output.

cluster

Optional name of a column identifying clusters for cluster-robust inference.

...

Additional arguments passed to [survival::coxph()] (e.g. `ties = "efron"`).

Value

A data frame of class `c("catmech_pooled_coxph", "data.frame")` containing:

term

Model coefficient names.

estimate

Pooled log hazard ratio parameter estimate.

std.error

Total pooled standard error.

df

Barnard & Rubin adjusted degrees of freedom.

lower, upper

Confidence interval bounds on the log hazard scale.

estimate_exp, lower_exp, upper_exp

Exponentiated parameters and bounds (Hazard Ratios) if `exponentiate = TRUE`.

within_variance

Average within-imputation variance.

between_variance

Between-imputation variance.

m, n, nevent

Number of completions, total observations, and events.

interpretation

Inference label.

Details

When the audited value is an analysis predictor, the imputation model needs the outcome: include the event indicator and the Nelson-Aalen cumulative hazard, which [mice::nelsonaalen()] computes, among the imputation `predictors` (White and Royston, 2009, <doi:10.1002/sim.3618>). A warning is given when the event indicator is missing. The complete-data degrees of freedom are events minus coefficients, the same default that `mice::pool()` uses for Cox fits.

Examples

set.seed(123)
n <- 50
df <- data.frame(
  time = stats::rexp(n, 0.1),
  status = stats::rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),
  lab = stats::rnorm(n, 10, 2),
  age = stats::rnorm(n, 50, 10)
)
df$lab_ref <- df$lab
df$lab_ref[11:n] <- NA
# lab is a predictor below, so the event indicator and the Nelson-Aalen
# cumulative hazard join the imputation model.
df$hazard <- mice::nelsonaalen(df, time, status)
res <- catmech_reference(df, value = "lab", reference = "lab_ref",
                         predictors = c("age", "status", "hazard"), m = 2, seed = 1)
pooled_cox <- catmech_pool_coxph(res, survival::Surv(time, status) ~ lab + age,
                                 exponentiate = TRUE)
print(pooled_cox)
#> -- Catmech Pooled Cox PH Model --
#> Completions (m): 2 | Observations (n): 50 | Events: 27
#> 
#>  term estimate std.error     df   lower  upper estimate_exp lower_exp upper_exp
#>   lab   0.2459    0.2178 0.7791 -5.2787 5.7706       1.2788    0.0051  320.7235
#>   age   0.0525    0.0866 0.6032 -5.6907 5.7957       1.0539    0.0034  328.8758
